title: SplatLab parametric archetype v1 — lathe with radial features
description: A DETERMINISTIC build recipe for a scan-guided clean solid. A model (or a human) fills in numbers; parametric_build.py turns numbers into geometry. Nothing here is geometry or code — that separation is what keeps the output editable, re-runnable and reviewable. Every length is in METRES in the object's own model frame: z = 0 at grade (the underside of the base flange), +z up, azimuth measured CCW from +x. Heights measured off an object-lane mesh are in THAT mesh's frame, which usually includes a ground slab — subtract provenance.grade_offset_m before writing them here, or the features land too high (this has already cost one build: the nozzles ended up on the dome).

schema_version.description: Exact version tag. A different value must be rejected, not coerced.

archetype.description: The only archetype v1 knows how to build: a solid of revolution plus radial features, optional flange bolt ring, optional crown nut.

name.description: Slug for the built object and its material names. kebab/snake, lower case.

units.description: v1 is metric-only. Declaring it makes an unconverted scan-unit instance a loud failure rather than a 2x-scale surprise.

lathe.description: Radial segments of the body revolve. 72 = 5 deg, the proven default.

feature.description: Radial segments of feature tubes (necks, caps). 24 is the proven default.

shade_auto_smooth_deg.description: Smooth-by-angle threshold. 40 keeps the barrel round while leaving flange/collar edges crisp.

materials.description: Material ROLES, keyed by role name (body, cap, metal, ...). Features and hardware reference these role names. Every declared role MUST receive geometry — an unused role is a schema/reality mismatch and is rejected, not silently dropped by the exporter.

profile.description: The lathe profile: an ordered (radius, height) polyline revolved about +z. MUST start and end on the axis (radius 0) so the solid is closed. Heights are non-decreasing and measured from grade. This is where a measured radius-vs-height table goes, verbatim.

features.description: Radial features (nozzles, bosses) attached to the body surface. Azimuth and height come from radial lobe analysis of the scan; form and colour role come from the photo.

flange_bolts.description: Bolt ring on the base flange, or explicit null for 'this archetype has no flange bolts'. The key is REQUIRED so 'no bolts' is a decision on the record rather than an omission.

crown_nut.description: Operating nut on the crown, or explicit null. Note: on a scan the nut is usually fused into the dome and already present in the measured profile — adding one then double-counts the height. Null is the correct value for a purely measured instance.

provenance.description: Where the numbers came from. Not decoration: grade_offset_m is the single value that most often ruins a build.

method.description: How this instance was produced, e.g. 'parametric_build.py measure v1' or 'vision model from crop.png + measured profile'.

source.description: The artifact the numbers were read off — usually an object-lane mesh path, plus the photo used for form.

meters_per_unit.description: Scene-unit -> metre calibration applied to the source, or null when the source was already metric. Recorded so a re-measure is reproducible.

grade_offset_m.description: Height of grade in the SOURCE mesh's own frame, already subtracted from every height in this instance. An object-lane mesh normally carries a ground slab; leaving this at 0 when the slab is present is the trap that puts nozzles on the dome.

notes.description: Free text — especially anything a downstream reviewer must not assume was measured.

measurement.description: Free-form receipt of the measurement pass (axis, centre, band size, estimator percentiles, detected lobes). Unconstrained on purpose: it records, it does not restrict.

slot.description: Material slot index on the joined object. Slots must be unique and contiguous from 0 so the build order (and therefore the exported material order) is deterministic.

base_color.description: Linear RGBA. A colour sampled off the scan is SHADED albedo and reads darker than the real paint; lift it deliberately if you want the painted look.

source.description: Where the colour came from. 'assumed' is legal but must be stated.

r.description: Radius from the axis, metres. 0 closes the solid (first and last point must be 0).

z.description: Height above grade, metres. Non-decreasing along the array.

note.description: Optional: why this control point is where it is.

type.description: 'nozzle' = neck + collar + cap + nut. 'boss' = neck only; its cap_* and nut_* fields MUST be null.

azimuth_deg.description: CCW from +x in the model frame, degrees. From the scan's radial lobes.

height_m.description: Axis height of the feature centreline ABOVE GRADE. Must sit on the body: the profile radius there has to exceed the neck radius.

inset_m.description: How far inside the body surface the neck starts, so it merges instead of floating. ~1/3 of the local body radius works.

neck_length_m.description: Radial reach of the neck from the body surface.

collar_radius_scale.description: Collar ridge radius as a multiple of the neck radius. 1.0 = no visible ridge.

body_material.description: Role name for the neck and collar. Must exist in materials.

cap_material.description: Role name for the cap; null only for type 'boss'.

nut_material.description: Role name for the cap nut; null only for type 'boss'.

evidence.description: Free-form: the lobe statistics this feature came from (bands, span, reach, prominence).

count.description: A TSDF scan of a painted hydrant does not resolve individual bolt heads — this is normally a photo or operator value, so say so in derivation.source.

circle_radius_m.description: Bolt-circle radius. Must fit inside the flange rim (circle + head <= max profile radius).

seat_height_m.description: Height of the flange top face the heads stand on.

sides.description: 5 = the pentagon operating nut on most municipal hydrants.

seat_inset_m.description: How far below the profile apex the nut is seated so it does not float.
